history.summary: Shakti temple at Hatimura, Silghat (Nagaon district), on the south bank of the Brahmaputra. Built during the reign of Ahom king Pramatta Singha (r. 1744-1751) in 1667 Sakabda, i.e. 1745-46 CE (the two datings are consistent). The presiding goddess is Durga worshipped as Mahisamardini (Mahishasuramardini), slayer of the buffalo demon. It was an important centre of Shaktism in ancient Assam; secondary sources state human sacrifice was once made at its altars, an unverified historical claim that is flagged. The current structure is in the indigenous Assamese/Ahom temple style. Town corrected from CSV 'Nagaon' to 'Silghat'.

name: Hatimura Temple
town_description: Silghat is a historic river-port town in the Kaliabor subdivision of Nagaon district, on the southern bank of the Brahmaputra. It is known for its cluster of old temples — the Kamakhya temple (called the second Kamakhya of Assam), the Trishuldhari Shiva temple and the Hatimura Shakti temple — and as a popular picnic spot with views of the Silghat hills.
